The system is designed to cut a carcass by using a movable support assembly that carries and positions cutting components relative to different portions of the carcass. The movable support assembly is arranged to travel along defined paths so that the cutting tools can be accurately guided during processing.

In operation, the support assembly moves along a first path positioned adjacent to a first portion of the carcass. While travelling along this first path, the support assembly enables a retractable assembly to extend toward the carcass. This extension places a first cutting tool in an operative position so that it can engage and process the first portion of the carcass as the support assembly advances along the first path.

After the first portion has been processed, the support assembly moves along a second path positioned adjacent to a second portion of the carcass. During movement along this second path, the retractable assembly retracts away from the carcass. As a result, the first cutting tool is disengaged from the carcass and does not interfere with processing of the second portion.

A second cutting tool is provided to process the second portion of the carcass while the support assembly travels along the second path. The first cutting tool is configured to move independently from the second cutting tool, allowing each tool to be positioned and operated according to the specific requirements of the carcass portion being processed. This arrangement enables efficient and controlled cutting of multiple carcass portions while reducing interference between the cutting tools.
outputs.L4:
A carcass-cutting system is provided for processing different portions of an animal carcass in a controlled and sequential manner. The system includes a support assembly configured to move relative to the carcass along at least two separate paths, each path corresponding to a different carcass portion or cutting operation. By guiding the support assembly along distinct paths, the system can accurately position cutting equipment for targeted engagement with selected areas of the carcass.

The system further includes a retractable assembly that carries or positions a first cutting tool. During movement of the support assembly along a first path, the retractable assembly advances the first cutting tool into an operative position so that it can engage and cut a first portion of the carcass. When the support assembly moves along a second path, the retractable assembly withdraws the first cutting tool into a non-operative or retracted position. This prevents the first cutting tool from contacting portions of the carcass that are not intended to be cut by that tool.

A second cutting tool is also provided for processing another portion of the carcass. The second cutting tool may operate while the first cutting tool is retracted, allowing the system to perform a different cutting operation on a different carcass area without interference from the first tool. Because the cutting tools can be moved and controlled independently, each tool can be brought into engagement only when needed and removed from the cutting zone when its operation is complete.

This arrangement enables sequential and targeted processing of multiple carcass regions using separate cutting tools suited to different cuts or anatomical areas. It reduces the risk of unintended tool engagement, improves accuracy, and allows the cutting sequence to be carried out more efficiently. As a result, the system provides improved cutting control, better carcass handling, and increased processing reliability in automated or semi-automated meat-processing operations.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. As a definite article, “the” helps us identify a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, saying “a book” could refer to any book, but saying “the book” tells us that both the speaker and listener know which book is being discussed.

This simple word adds clarity and precision to sentences. It guides readers and listeners by pointing to something particular. Whether we say “the sun,” “the ocean,” or “the best moment,” the word creates a sense of focus and importance.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential to English grammar. Without it, many sentences would feel incomplete or unclear. Its frequent use shows that even the smallest words can have great meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an automated carcass cutting system with movable support, retractable assembly, and independently movable first and second cutting tools.
counterfactuals.output: An automated carcass cutting system includes a movable support configured to carry at least a portion of a carcass along a processing path and a retractable cutting assembly positioned adjacent the processing path. The retractable cutting assembly is selectively movable between an operative position, in which the assembly is positioned for cutting engagement with the carcass, and a retracted position spaced from the carcass. The cutting assembly includes a first cutting tool and a second cutting tool, each independently movable relative to the support and relative to one another. A controller is configured to actuate movement of the support, the retractable cutting assembly, and the first and second cutting tools according to a cutting sequence, such that the cutting tools perform respective cuts on the carcass while accommodating variations in carcass size, shape, or position. An invention is provided for processing an animal carcass by cutting different portions of the carcass along two adjacent paths. The system includes a carcass support or conveyor 12 configured to position and advance the carcass, a sensing or positioning assembly 14 configured to identify a cutting location or anatomical reference, and a cutting assembly 16 arranged to perform controlled cuts on the carcass. A controller 18 is operatively connected to the sensing assembly 14 and the cutting assembly 16 to guide the cutting assembly 16 along first and second adjacent cutting paths.

In use, the carcass is positioned by the support 12, and the sensing assembly 14 determines the location of portions to be separated. The controller 18 directs the cutting assembly 16 to cut a first portion of the carcass along a first path and a second portion of the carcass along an adjacent second path. counterfactuals.output:
A carcass cutting apparatus comprising:

a support assembly configured to support at least a portion of an animal carcass, the support assembly being movable relative to a frame of the apparatus;

a first cutting tool arranged to cut a first portion of the carcass, the first cutting tool being movable between an extended cutting position and a retracted non-cutting position; and

a second cutting tool arranged to cut a second portion of the carcass different from the first portion;

wherein the first cutting tool and the second cutting tool are independently movable relative to one another and relative to the support assembly so as to permit separate positioning and operation of the first and second cutting tools during cutting of the carcass.

In one embodiment, the support assembly is movable along a guide path to position the carcass relative to the first and second cutting tools. The first cutting tool may be selectively advanced toward the carcass to perform a first cutting operation and subsequently retracted away from the carcass. The second cutting tool may be separately actuated to perform a second cutting operation on another portion of the carcass before, during, or after movement of the first cutting tool.

The apparatus may further comprise one or more actuators operatively coupled to the support assembly, the first cutting tool, and the second cutting tool, respectively, such that movement of each of the support assembly, the first cutting tool, and the second cutting tool is independently controllable. The first cutting tool may comprise a blade, saw, knife, rotary cutter, or other cutting member, and the second cutting tool may comprise a separate blade, saw, knife, rotary cutter, or other cutting member configured for cutting a different carcass portion.
